kept.reason: No assertion maps onto put_list_get_env_rm_a_profile: that test checks a profile's put/get/env/rm round trip against a reachable vault; this one checks pending writes kept on this host while every Core method is rate-limited, list's pending marks, and the push keeping another host's Field. Folding the failing-vault setup into the round trip would change what it checks.

Setups conflict: folding 'a read warns of what waits' and 'the next --now write pushes it' into a_write_the_vault_cannot_take_now_waits_and_the_next_sync_pushes_it was tried; after that test's another-token steps a read no longer warns and a --now write leaves 2 writes waiting, so the fold changes what one half checks (its list --fresh push or the other-token reads).

kept_files.reason: Deep enough: the pure core of a Secret (Name, Kind, Values, Field, Fault) and the decisions put/get/env/list make on it behind a few functions (parse_set/parse_meta/stdin_value/pipe_field for put's inputs, merge, value, to_json/summary, exports), each doing real work (merge finds every fault at once and upserts Fields in order). Callers in commands.rs/item.rs/store.rs use only that interface; tests reach no private helper. Size is ~60 lines of Fault docs (the manual's refusal table) plus refusal wording; churn is features adding inputs and faults to the domain core, which belong here. Splitting put's input parsing out would spread one concept over two modules for no leverage.
